prize_parts.citation: For discoveries of GLP-1 physiology and the identification of the active peptide that enabled incretin-based therapies for diabetes and obesity

statement.case_for: All six openings ranked B013 first, but I do not treat that as evidence of merit. The merit is independent. GLP-1 physiology is a complete chain from hormone biology to drug: Holst's work on secretion and action, Drucker's work on proglucagon-derived peptide biology and mechanism, and the identification and synthesis of the active peptide form. That chain produced therapies with documented glycaemic, weight, cardiovascular and renal benefit in large outcome trials, and it has been confirmed independently for roughly two decades. It is mature, original and of very large impact. A prize built around the discovery side (physiology, peptide identity, mechanism) keeps the award on scientific discovery, while the citation can still acknowledge the therapeutic consequence.
statement.case_against: The credit is crowded and contested. Four names are credited and the cap is three, so any configuration excludes someone with a real claim. Mojsov's priority relative to others in the early 1980s is debated and I cannot verify it from the supplied record. Knudsen's liraglutide and semaglutide work is what actually reached patients at scale, and leaving her out will be read as favouring discovery over development. Industrial drug development also blurs where basic discovery ends. If the committee cannot agree on a defensible three, B042 or B008 may be easier to attribute, even though I rate their overall impact lower.

responses.point: Perlmann proposed Drucker, Holst and Knudsen, treating Knudsen's long-acting acylated analogues as the step that made the biology into a drug, and ranked HPV VLP vaccines third.
responses.response: I take the Knudsen argument seriously: without long-acting analogues the physiology would not have changed clinical practice. But a prize that rewards the engineering of a specific drug sits less comfortably with the discovery criterion than one that rewards identification of the peptide. I would hold Mojsov in the trio, accepting that her priority is contested, because the active-peptide identification is what made every later analogue possible. I disagree on that weighting, but I agree with Perlmann that the exclusion needs to be stated openly. On HPV, I rank it lower than he does because the priority disputes among the parallel VLP groups and the omission of Jian Zhou make a clean three-person attribution harder.

responses.point: Wahren-Herlenius also put Drucker, Holst and Knudsen first, said the three-person cap forces an unresolved Mojsov question, and ranked BCR-ABL inhibition (B012) third, ahead of CAR-T.
responses.response: We agree on the core B013 pair and differ only on the third name, so the disagreement is narrow. I do not agree that B012 should outrank CAR-T. Imatinib is exemplary, but the compound, clinical proof and resistance work sit on top of earlier BCR-ABL fusion discoveries outside the credit set, and the novelty of the claim is lower. CAR-T opens a new modality, and its attribution problem (Eshhar outside the credited names) is serious but a different kind of problem.

responses.point: Linnarsson placed the cell-free fetal DNA work (B005) second, as a single-person configuration for Lo with worldwide clinical effect.
responses.response: B005 has a clean one-person attribution and a very real clinical effect, and I accept that. I still rank it below B042 and B008 because the impact is mostly in screening and diagnostics, and its performance limits (false positives, placental mosaicism) are practical. A single-person award would also leave out the sequencing enablers that Linnarsson himself says are separate. I would not move it ahead of a therapy that cures or transforms disease, but I would keep it in view if the committee wants a compact second part.

responses.point: Sandberg ranked HPV VLP vaccines second and CAR-T third, and treated Drucker, Holst and Mojsov as the strongest scientific trio.
responses.response: I share his trio for B013 and his reasoning that physiology and peptide identification are the decisive scientific contributions. Where I differ is on putting HPV above CAR-T. The cancer-incidence evidence for HPV vaccination is strong and growing, but the VLP priority question is unresolved and the credited trio omits Zhou. I put CAR-T above it, with the caveat that the same Eshhar problem weakens that ranking.

uncertainties: Whether the committee will accept Mojsov in place of Knudsen, and how much weight to give Mojsov's contested early-1980s priority.
Whether a second distinct achievement (for example B042 or B008) should share the prize, or whether the three-person cap makes B013 alone the cleaner configuration.
For B042, how to handle foundational CAR concept credit (Eshhar) outside the supplied names.
For B008, whether the prize would be read as recognising splicing biology or antisense chemistry, and the omission of other co-inventors.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from the provided profile for the shortlisted candidates. My documented connections are my postdoctoral period with Paul Greengard and roughly twenty co-authored works with Thomas Perlmann (not independently audited), and neither involves a credited name on any shortlisted ballot. My neurology background touches B025, which I did not rank first, and I have no documented tie to its credited names.
